description: The bar chart illustrates the number of datasets published per year from 2012 to 2022, categorized by two data sources labeled “1” (blue bars) and an unlabeled source (orange bars), with a third category represented by light gray bars in 2022 only. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” ranges from 0 to 100 in increments of 20, while the horizontal axis displays years chronologically from 2012 to 2022. Dataset counts are minimal in the early years: in 2012–2015, only one or two datasets appear per year, mostly from source “1.” From 2016 onward, the number of datasets increases steadily, with source “1” consistently contributing more datasets than the orange source until 2022. In 2020, source “1” peaks at approximately 85 datasets, while the orange source reaches about 43. In 2021, source “1” surges to over 100 datasets (approximately 110), and the orange source reaches about 45. In 2022, the blue bar drops to around 30, the orange bar to about 7, and a new light gray bar appears at approximately 10, indicating a third data source not present in prior years. The chart visually emphasizes the dramatic growth in dataset availability, particularly from source “1,” peaking in 2021, followed by a sharp decline in 2022.
